content:
Connor O'Brien: Heads up: runtime-1.19 branch cut is tomorrow 10:00 PT. We can still land the mixed-workload scheduler *flag plumbing* (default-off) if we’re confident it’s safe. Key requirement: stays default-off everywhere unless explicitly enabled via ops config. Can we confirm what’s merging + what needs to be held for 1.20?

Sofia Ivanova: For 1.19 I only want PR #8421 (flag + config surface) and maybe #8471 (docs/comments) if it’s low risk. The actual scheduling policy (#8433/#8439) can stay behind the flag and land later, but I’d rather not rush it into the release branch.

Benji Okafor: +1. For 1.19 we should keep it as “wiring only” unless we’re sure the code path is dead when disabled. What’s the flag name right now?

Marcus Reed: In #8421 it’s `runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.enabled` (bool). Defaults false. Also guard is checked at scheduler init, so when false it instantiates the existing FIFO scheduler.

Connor O'Brien: Cool. Two questions:
1) Is there any way for tenants/customers to toggle it (headers, request params, etc.)?
2) What’s the config precedence order in Dedicated vs Hosted? I want to ensure no accidental enable from old configs.

Benji Okafor: 1) No, not request-level. It’s runtime config only.
2) Precedence: compiled defaults < environment/runtime config file < control-plane override (for Hosted) or cluster config (Dedicated). But since default is false, it only flips if someone sets it true explicitly.

Paula Mendes: From product/rollouts side: for 1.19 release notes we should explicitly state “feature-flagged, default off, not supported for general availability”. Also we should align on who has permission to flip it in prod (SRE only?) for canary.

Rafael Mendes: SRE perspective: default-off is necessary but not sufficient. I want a guardrail that prevents enabling it on full fleet accidentally. Ideally we restrict to allowlist of clusters / routes until canary is complete.

Marcus Reed: There’s a “scope” key in the config system but #8421 didn’t add allowlisting yet. We can keep enablement limited operationally by only setting it in perf-canary and a single Dedicated canary cluster. But yeah, the system itself won’t stop a bad config push.

Tomáš Novák: If we’re not shipping the scheduler behavior in 1.19, could we still add a safety “deny in prod” check? Like require `runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.allow_prod_enable=true` as a second key? That’s cheap and blocks fat-finger.

Sofia Ivanova: That’s a good idea but might be too much churn for the branch cut. Also if we add a second key, we need to document it and make sure operators don’t get confused.

Connor O'Brien: Given timing: let’s keep 1.19 minimal. But I do want a release checklist item: “Verify mixed workload scheduler flag remains false in all standard configs”. Rafael/Tomáš can you add a quick check in the rollout monitoring checklist?

Rafael Mendes: Yup. We can add an assertion in the runtime config diff tool we run during release candidate validation. At minimum, a grep in the rendered config artifacts for `mixed_workload.enabled: true` should be empty.

Benji Okafor: Also we can add a unit/integration test in runtime that fails if default value changes. Something like `EXPECT_FALSE(Config::GetBool("runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.enabled"))`.

Marcus Reed: Already in #8421 there’s a basic integration test that loads default config and expects the legacy scheduler type. It indirectly checks the flag default. I can make it explicit if you want.

Connor O'Brien: That’s good enough for 1.19. Keep it low-risk.

Paula Mendes: Re release notes: can we keep the wording precise? Something like: “Introduced feature flag plumbing for mixed-workload scheduler prototype (off by default). No behavior change unless enabled.”

Sofia Ivanova: Yes. And we should call out that it is intended for perf-canary only initially.

Connor O'Brien: Action items:
- Marcus: confirm #8421 is green on main + no pending migrations. Drop link here.
- Sofia: confirm no behavior PRs are being cherry-picked to 1.19.
- Benji: sanity check config key naming conventions (under `runtime.scheduler.*`) and that the flag is not exposed via user API.
- Rafael/Tomáš: add release validation check + note for on-call.

Marcus Reed: #8421 is green: https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/8421 (merged, CI passed). No schema migrations. Only config + feature flag check + small test.

Benji Okafor: Looked at it. Key name OK. It’s in the “internal runtime config” namespace, not surfaced in public docs. Control plane doesn’t expose it to customers.

Sofia Ivanova: Confirmed: we will not cherry-pick #8433/#8439 into 1.19 branch. Those will land on main behind the flag and will be enabled only in perf-canary via config.

Tomáš Novák: I’ll add the check to the release runbook + ping Rafael once PR is up.

Rafael Mendes: Also request: once the 1.19 RC is cut, can you post the exact config key path in #eng-sre so we can add an alert / dashboard annotation when it flips in canary?

Marcus Reed: Yep. It’s `runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload.enabled`. When true, runtime logs `scheduler_mode=mixed_workload` at startup (info level). I can add a sampled log line too but that’s separate.

Connor O'Brien: Perfect. For branch cut: I’m tagging this as “safe to include in runtime-1.19”. Please don’t sneak in behavior changes under the same flag in the release branch.

ReleaseBot: Release train update: runtime-1.19 branch cut scheduled. Freeze begins at 2024-11-13 18:00 UTC. Approved cherry-picks must be labeled `release-1.19`.

Paula Mendes: Thanks. I’ll draft the release note snippet for runtime-1.19 and send to Connor for review.

Connor O'Brien: Last call: any concerns about the flag existing in 1.19 even if unused?

Rafael Mendes: Only that someone turns it on without dashboards. But we’re adding the config diff check + we can keep enabling gated to perf-canary cluster. So OK.

Sofia Ivanova: Agreed. Also the docs PR (#8471) can wait; we can keep operator enablement instructions internal until canary is done.

Connor O'Brien: Sounds good. Thread closed unless something blows up in RC.

Tomáš Novák: :thumbsup: will follow up in #eng-sre with the validation snippet once merged.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup:
